BOND¶

BOND (Bed of Nails Design) is Sistemi’s open source PCBA tester. It is a Teensy 4.1 based jig controller with four headers of configurable analog and digital pins, a DUT power supply, a battery emulator, and pass/fail LEDs. You design a Pogo board, with the spring probes for your DUT, that plugs into the BOND headers.

  • Product brief: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/a4402-SPC_ProductBrief_01.pdf

  • Schematic: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/a4402-SCH_05.pdf

  • Driver developer guide: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/README.md

  • Example scripts and test code: public/prism/scripts/example/BOND_v0

  • Pogo board template: a5800-BONDPogo, see Designing the Pogo Board

Getting Started¶

  1. Program the BOND firmware into a new BOND, with the example script bond_progfresh_0.scr, or with the Arduino IDE, see public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/server/README.md. Only one BOND may be plugged in while programming.

  2. With no Pogo board or DUT connected, run the self test script bond_selftest_0.scr. It checks the BOND supplies, the header ADCs against the 2.5V reference, the battery emulator and the DUT supply.

  3. Copy the example folder to your product, for example public/prism/scripts/myproduct/BLT, and change the scripts and test code, see the example’s README.md. The P1000-P1999 test items are examples, add your own tests after them.

bond_update_0.scr updates the firmware of a BOND that is already programmed. Run it only once per Prism start, as the BOND’s USB port can change after the update. The Arduino IDE must be closed while Prism uses BOND.

Designing the Pogo Board¶

Start your Pogo board from Sistemi’s template, the Altium Designer project a5800-BONDPogo. It has the four BOND headers already placed where they mate with BOND, a spring pin part, the BOND schematic and a 3D model of BOND. You add the spring pins for your DUT’s test points, and wire each one to a header pin. The template’s README.md lists its files.

The stack up, from the top,

  • the DUT, with its test points facing down,

  • the spring pins, on the Pogo board,

  • the Pogo board, with the four headers TH1-TH4 (Molex 90151-2120) on its bottom side,

  • BOND, with its headers facing the Pogo board, and its components facing away from it.

Plan the test points and their header pins first, see PCBA Test Coverage, sections Pin Budget, Test Point Location and From the Pin Map to the Pogo Board.

Start a Pogo Board Project¶

Your Pogo board is usually private, and a GitHub fork of a public repo can’t be private. Clone the template, and push it to a new, empty private repo,

git clone https://github.com/sistemicorp/a5800-BONDPogo.git myproduct-Pogo
cd myproduct-Pogo
git remote rename origin sistemi
git remote add origin git@github.com:<your org>/myproduct-Pogo.git
git push -u origin master

The sistemi remote lets you fetch later changes to the template. In Altium, rename the project and the title blocks to your own part number.

Schematic¶

  • In Top.SchDoc, copy the spring pin TP1 once for each DUT test point. Name each after the test point and its net, for example TP1-VDD, TP2-IN5, the same as the Pin Map.

  • Use several GND spring pins, TPG1, TPG2…, spread over the DUT.

  • Connect each test point to a net of the header sheets TH1-TH4. Each sheet gives the BOND function and range of its pins, for example VDUT (1-20V, 1A), VBAT (2-5V, 0.8A), the open drain outputs, UART, I2C, JTAG/SWD and USB, and the general purpose PORT pins (ADC, DAC, GPO or GPI, set in the Header Definition File).

  • Circuits that BOND controls, such as switched loads, dividers or relays, go on the Pogo board too, see Pogo Board Circuits.

BOND has some flexibility: some header pins depend on how the BOND is populated, for example header 3 pin 2 to the BNC connector, or the divider on header 1 pin 8. Check your BOND against the BOND schematic public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/a4402-SCH_05.pdf, and change the template to match it.

Layout¶

  • Do not move the headers TH1-TH4, or change their footprints. They must line up with the BOND headers.

  • Place the spring pins under the DUT test points, from the DUT’s layout. Keep the trace from each spring pin to its header pin short, see Test Point Location.

  • The template board is 2 mm thick, which keeps the spring pins straight and the board flat under the force of the pins.

  • Parts on the top of the Pogo board must clear the DUT and the parts on its bottom side. The bottom of the Pogo board sits over BOND, keep it clear apart from the headers.

Stack Up STEP Model¶

The template layout has a 3D model of BOND (a4402-CAD_PCB1_01.step) mated to the Pogo board, and the template’s a5800-CAD_3DwBOND_01.step is the two boards together. Add the 3D model of your DUT on its spring pins, and export a STEP of the whole stack up, BOND, Pogo board and DUT. The jig’s mechanical design (the base, the DUT nest, the lid and its hold downs) starts from that model.

Mechanical¶

These are typical values, check them against the spring pin’s datasheet and your jig.

  • Spring pins: the template uses S13-503-SISTEMI. When the jig is closed, compress each pin to about two thirds of its travel, so every pin has force even when the DUT is not flat.

  • DUT test pads: about 1 mm across, at least 2.54 mm (100 mil) apart centre to centre where you can, 1.27 mm at the least. Keep pads a few mm from tall parts, and on one side of the DUT.

  • Alignment: two non-plated tooling holes on the DUT, at opposite corners, with guide pins in the nest or on the Pogo board. Pin to pad accuracy comes from the tooling holes, not the board edge.

  • Hold down: push the DUT down with hold down fingers in the lid, placed over the spring pins, so the DUT does not bend. Many spring pins add up to a large force.

  • Through hole connector pins and the programming header can be probed too, see PCBA Test Coverage.

Before ordering the Pogo board, check its schematic against the Pin Map and the header definition file, pin by pin.

Header Definition File¶

Each Pogo board has a header definition file, which sets how each header pin is used: ADC, DAC, GPO, GPI or not used. The file is given with the driver in the script config,

"config": {
  "fail_fast": true,
  "drivers": [["public.prism.drivers.A4401_BOND.hwdrv_A4401_BOND",
               "public/prism/scripts/myproduct/BLT/assets/pogo_hdr_definition._json"]]
},

  • Start from the example assets/pogo_hdr_definition._json, and use the BOND schematic Header # pages to map your Pogo board’s signals to header pins.

  • Each pin is {“mode”: <mode>, “port”: <port>}. A pin wired to two ports lists both, for example {“mode”: “ADC,GPO”, “port”: “6,9”}.

  • ADC and DAC ranges are 0-10000 mV. Each header has one GPO high level (gpo_mv) and one GPI threshold (gpi_mv).

  • HDR1 pin 1 is an adjustable LDO output (600-3900 mV), set with bond_ldo_set.

  • The file is checked when the driver loads, an invalid file fails the script Validate.

  • Different DUTs use different Pogo boards, each with its own file.

The full rules are in the driver README.md, section BOND Header Pin Configuration.

To plan which DUT test points go to which header pins, and the Pogo board circuits, see Pin Budget in PCBA Test Coverage.

Test Code¶

The setup item gets the BOND for its channel from the drivers, and records BOND’s id for traceability, see Traceability,

drivers = self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type=DRIVER_TYPE)
driver = drivers[0]
_, _, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("teensy4_id", driver["obj"]["unique_id"],
                                       ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING)
self.teensy = driver["obj"]["hwdrv"]

Each BOND method returns a dict, {‘success’: True, ‘method’: …, ‘result’: {…}}. Check success before using result,

response = self.teensy.bond_max_hdr_adc(hdr=1, pin=9)
if not response['success']:
    self.item_end(ResultAPI.RECORD_RESULT_INTERNAL_ERROR)
    return
success, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("v3v3", response['result']['mV'],
                                                   ResultAPI.UNIT_MILLIVOLTS,
                                                   ctx.item.args.min, ctx.item.args.max)

The main methods, see A4401_BOND.py for all of them and their arguments,

  • header pins: bond_max_hdr_adc, bond_max_hdr_dac, bond_max_hdr_gpo, bond_max_hdr_gpi

  • DUT supply: vdut_set, vdut_en, vdut_con, vdut_read, vdut_get_fault

  • battery emulator: vbat_set, vbat_read, iox_vbat_en, iox_vbat_con

  • other: bond_ldo_set, vbus_en, led, version, unique_id, temperature, reset

BOND is reset at the start and end of every test, which sets the DACs to 0V and the GPOs to their idle level. The BOND driver also gives Prism the jig closed detect (play) and the pass/fail LEDs (show_pass_fail), see Drivers.

Command Line¶

A4401_BOND_cli.py runs BOND methods without Prism, for bringing up a Pogo board and debugging,

cd ~/git/scripts/public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND
python A4401_BOND_cli.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 status
python A4401_BOND_cli.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 -n bond_max_hdr_adc_cal --header 3
python A4401_BOND_cli.py --help

Stop Prism, or close the script in Prism, before using the CLI, only one program can use the BOND serial port at a time.
